mainTopic: The end of רבי שמעון's ברייתא about backing out of a deal (the curse of 'מי שפרע' and 'אין רוח חכמים נוחה הימנו'), and the start of רבא's proof from a פסוק that supports ריש לקיש: by Torah law, money does not acquire movable items.
overview: This amud continues the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. רבי יוחנן holds that by Torah law, paying money acquires a movable item. ריש לקיש holds that only pulling the item (משיכה) acquires it. First the גמרא finishes רבי שמעון's ברייתא. Backing out after money was paid brings the curse of 'מי שפרע'. Backing out of a deal made only with words brings only the Sages' displeasure, and רבא confirms that the curse needs money to have been paid. Then רבא proves ריש לקיש's view from a פסוק. The return פסוק in ויקרא never openly names תשומת יד, because a vessel that was never pulled never became the lender's. That proof survives several challenges. Next comes support from a ברייתא. Paying a bathhouse attendant with הקדש money is מעילה right away, but buying an object is not מעילה until it is pulled. A barber who is a גוי is the exception. Finally, the גמרא brings the other side: רב נחמן says money acquires by Torah law, and לוי found a ברייתא where paying a wholesaler with הקדש money is מעילה even without pulling.

steps.title: Pulling the item closes the deal, but backing out after payment brings a curse
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says that pulling the item closes a deal and paying money does not. Even so, whoever backs out after money was paid falls under the curse of 'מי שפרע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: The Sages said that pulling a garment closes the deal, so the seller now owns the gold coin. Taking the gold coin does not close the deal, so the buyer does not yet own the garment. Even so, and even though that is the law, the Sages said this about someone who backs out: The One Who punished the generation of the flood, the generation of the dispersion, Sodom and Gomorrah, and the Egyptians at the sea will punish whoever does not keep his word.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing to quote a ברייתא with רבי שמעון's view. In a deal, pulling the item closes the sale, but paying money does not. Still, backing out after payment is morally serious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון agrees that legally, money alone does not close a deal on movable items, so either side can still back out. He adds a strong warning: a person who backs out after money has changed hands is under a heavenly curse. Legally the deal is open, but morally it is binding.

keyTerms.meaning: A garment (here, the item being sold)
"He Who punished". This is the opening of the curse against someone who backs out of a deal.
The generation of the dispersion (the Tower of Babel)

steps.confusionAlert: The curse does not mean the sale went through. Legally, the deal is still not done. The curse is a moral and heavenly punishment, not a court ruling.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Even though they said
a garment acquires a gold dinar
phrases.notes: Once the buyer pulls the garment, the deal is closed and the seller now owns the coin.

phrases.english: but a gold dinar does not acquire a garment,
in any case, that is the law.
But they said:
He Who punished the people of the generation of the flood
and the people of the generation of the dispersion
and the people of Sodom and Gomorrah
and the Egyptians at the sea
He will in the future punish
whoever does not stand by his word.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that the גמרא began quoting before this section, as part of the argument over whether money acquires.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pulling the item acquires it and money does not. But whoever backs out after money was paid falls under the curse of 'מי שפרע'.

steps.title: A deal made only with words
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that agreeing with words alone does not close a deal. But whoever backs out of it is someone the Sages are not pleased with.
steps.simpleTranslation: And someone who agrees to a deal with words alone has not acquired anything. But if he backs out, the Sages are not pleased with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second, lighter case. Two people agreed on a deal only with words, and no money was paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Words alone have no legal power to close a sale. Backing out is not cursed like the case with money. It is only something the Sages dislike. So we now have two levels: money paid brings the curse, and words alone bring the Sages' displeasure.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages are not pleased with him

phrases.english: And one who negotiates with words
has not acquired,
and one who backs out of it
the Sages are not pleased with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the same ברייתא with a lighter case: words alone, with no money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Words alone do not acquire. Backing out is not cursed, but the Sages are displeased.

steps.title: רבא explains when the curse applies
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that backing out of words alone gets only 'the Sages are not pleased'. The curse of 'אבל אמרו' applies only when money was paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: For someone who backs out of words alone, we have only "the Sages are not pleased with him." If there were words and money was also paid, he is under the "But they said" curse. If there were words and no money was paid, he is not under the "But they said" curse.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא clarifies where the line is between the curse and the Sages' displeasure. That line depends on whether money was paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that breaking any promise brings the curse. רבא says no: the curse needs money to have changed hands. Without money, the most the person gets is the Sages' displeasure.

keyTerms.meaning: He is under the "But". This means the curse that begins "But they said".

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels. Pulling the item makes it a full legal sale. Paying money is not legally binding, but backing out brings the curse of 'מי שפרע'. Words alone are not binding, and backing out brings only 'אין רוח חכמים נוחה הימנו'.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
We have nothing but
"the Sages are not pleased with him."
Words, and there is money along with them
he stands under the "But".
phrases.notes: The "But" is the curse from step 1 that began "But they said: He Who punished..."

phrases.english: Words, and there is no money along with them
he does not stand under the "But".

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: אָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the two parts of the ברייתא fit together.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The curse applies only when money was paid. With words alone, backing out brings only the Sages' displeasure.

steps.title: רבא brings a פסוק to support ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רבא announces that a פסוק and a ברייתא support ריש לקיש. He starts by quoting the פסוק about a person who falsely denies something to his fellow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A פסוק and a ברייתא support ריש לקיש. The פסוק is the one that says: "And he denies to his fellow about a deposit, or a pledge, or a robbery, or oppressed his fellow."
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. רבא is setting up a proof for ריש לקיש, who holds that by Torah law money does not acquire movable items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we had the ברייתא of רבי שמעון. Now רבא opens a fresh line of support. He quotes the פסוק first, and the explanation of how it proves the point comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה)
A deposit left with someone to look after

phrases.english: Rava said:
A verse and a baraita
support Reish Lakish.
The verse, as it is written:
"And he denies to his fellow about a deposit
or a pledge, or a robbery
or oppressed his fellow."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, קְרָא וּמַתְנִיתָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new proof in the larger argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's view that by Torah law, money does not acquire movable items
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 5:21 (and a ברייתא that comes later)

steps.title: רב חסדא explains 'pledge' and 'oppressed'
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that both 'תשומת יד' and 'עשק' in the פסוק are cases where a specific vessel was set aside: one for a loan, the other for wages.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Pledge": רב חסדא said, this is a case where the borrower set aside a vessel for his loan. "Oppressed": רב חסדא said, this is a case where the employer set aside a vessel for the worker, and then oppressed him by not paying.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא defines two words in the פסוק. This prepares the proof that רבא will build next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about denying a specific item, like a deposit, and not just a debt. So רב חסדא explains that both cases involve a specific vessel that was set aside. That makes them cases about an actual object, which is what the proof will need.

keyTerms.meaning: A pledge; something set aside to back up a loan
Oppressed; here, held back a worker's pay
He set aside a vessel for him

phrases.english: "Pledge"
Rav Chisda said:
such as where he set aside a vessel for his loan.
"Oppressed"
Rav Chisda said:
such as where he set aside a vessel for him for his oppression.
phrases.notes: An employer set aside a vessel to back up the worker's wages, and then held back the pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines words in the פסוק that רבא just quoted, as a setup for the proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'תשומת יד' is a vessel set aside for a loan. 'עשק' is a vessel set aside for a worker's wages.

steps.title: The return verse skips the pledge because it was never pulled
steps.stepSummary: The 'return' פסוק lists גזלה, עושק and פקדון again but leaves out תשומת יד. רבא says the reason is that the lender never pulled the vessel, so it is not his.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק lists again what the person must give back, it mentions the stolen item, the withheld wages, and the deposit. It does not mention the pledge (the loan). Why? Isn't it because the lender never pulled the vessel, so he never owned it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes the proof from the פסוק. The 'giving back' verse repeats three of the four cases but skips תשומת יד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said that תשומת יד and עושק both involve a vessel that was set aside. In תשומת יד the vessel was set aside for a loan, but the lender never pulled it. Since there was no משיכה, the vessel never became the lender's, so there is no item to 'give back'. This shows that without pulling there is no acquisition, which fits ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: the פסוק repeated it (listed it again)
a loan with a vessel set aside for it (a 'pledge')

phrases.english: And when the verse repeats them, it is written:
"And it shall be, if he has sinned and is guilty,
that he shall return the stolen item that he stole,
or the withheld item that he withheld,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֶת הַפִּקָּדוֹן אֲשֶׁר הׇפְקַד אִתּוֹ״,
phrases.english: or the deposit that was deposited with him,"
while the pledge, it does not repeat.
What is the reason?
Is it not because it is missing pulling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב חסדא's explanation (vessel set aside) to complete רבא's proof from the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש: by Torah law only משיכה acquires, not money.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 5:23 leaves out תשומת יד when listing what must be returned.

steps.title: רב פפא: withheld wages had no pulling either, yet the verse repeats it
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רבא: עושק also involves a vessel that was set aside but not pulled, and the פסוק does repeat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: Look at the withheld wages. The פסוק does list them again, even though there was no pulling there either!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks רבא's proof. He points to עושק, which looks just like תשומת יד, yet the פסוק repeats it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב חסדא, עושק is also a case of a vessel set aside, here for a worker's wages, with no pulling. If the פסוק still says to 'return' it, then missing משיכה cannot be the reason תשומת יד was left out. So the proof for ריש לקיש falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: withholding what is owed, here a worker's wages

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
Say, look at the withheld wages: the verse does repeat it!
phrases.notes: Like the pledge, the wages vessel was only set aside and never pulled, yet the פסוק still lists it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא אֵימָא מֵעוֹשֶׁק הוּא דְּאַהְדַּר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that תשומת יד was left out because it lacks משיכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עושק also lacks משיכה, yet it is repeated, so lack of pulling cannot explain the omission.

steps.title: The withheld wages case is one where the worker took the item and gave it back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the עושק in the return פסוק is a case where the worker took the vessel (pulling it) and then deposited it back with the employer.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we talking about here? A case where the worker took the item from the employer, and then gave it back to him to hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא's proof. It explains the עושק case so that there was pulling after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the worker took the vessel, so he pulled it and acquired it. Then he left it with the employer, who denied having it. So a real item belonging to the worker is being denied, and that is why it must be 'returned'. This fits ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with here?
and then he deposited it back with him

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where he took it from him,
phrases.notes: The worker took the vessel from the employer, so he pulled it.

phrases.english: and then deposited it back with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עושק in the return פסוק was never pulled.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worker did pull it and then deposited it back, so it was truly his.

steps.title: That would just be a deposit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that if the worker deposited the item, it is simply a פקדון, which the פסוק already lists.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is just the same as a deposit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. If the item was deposited, why does the פסוק need to list it separately as עושק?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already says 'or the deposit'. If עושק here means an item deposited with the employer, it seems to repeat the פקדון case for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: an item left with someone to watch

phrases.english: That is the same as a deposit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case explanation of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that עושק means an item taken and deposited back.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That case is already covered by the word פקדון, so the פסוק would be repeating itself.

steps.title: There are two kinds of deposit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק lists two different kinds of פקדון: a regular one, and one where the item first came from the person now holding it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two kinds of deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two words cover two different deposit cases, so nothing is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'פקדון' is a normal deposit. 'עושק' is a deposit of an item that first came from the holder himself, the employer, and was then left back with him. Since these are different situations, the פסוק mentions both.

phrases.english: There are two kinds of deposit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עושק as a deposit is just a repeat of פקדון.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a second, different type of deposit, so the פסוק needs both words.

steps.title: Then the verse could have repeated the pledge the same way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if so, the פסוק could also have repeated תשומת יד and explained it as a case where the lender took the vessel and deposited it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is true, let the פסוק also list the pledge again. We could explain it as a case where the lender took the item from the borrower and then left it back with him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer against רבא's proof. The same trick could have worked for תשומת יד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק can talk about a 'taken and deposited back' case for עושק, it could have done the same for תשומת יד. Then the fact that תשומת יד is left out does not seem to prove anything about משיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: let us explain it as a specific case

phrases.english: If so,
let it repeat the pledge too,
and explain it as a case where he took it from him
phrases.notes: Here it is the lender who pulls the vessel from the borrower.

phrases.english: and then deposited it back with him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי תְּשׂוּמֶת יָד נָמֵי לַיהְדְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of steps 8 and 10 to question the proof of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's proof from the omission of תשומת יד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק could have included תשומת יד with the same explanation, so its absence seems to show nothing.

steps.title: Leaving out the pledge is what supports ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if the פסוק had repeated תשומת יד, it would prove nothing either way. Since it did not repeat it, that silence supports ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק had listed the pledge again, it would be neither a disproof nor a proof. But now that the פסוק did not list it, it supports ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the proof still stands and closes the discussion: the leaving out of תשומת יד is what supports ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Had תשומת יד been listed, we could have explained it as a 'taken and deposited back' case, so it would prove nothing. But it was left out, and the simplest reason is that a vessel never pulled was never acquired. So the omission supports the view that only משיכה acquires.

keyTerms.meaning: now (that this is how it is)

steps.whatToRemember: The return פסוק leaves out תשומת יד because the set-aside vessel was never pulled. This silence supports ריש לקיש that by Torah law משיכה, not money, closes a deal.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof does not come from what the פסוק says, but from what it leaves out. Including תשומת יד would not have disproved ריש לקיש, but leaving it out supports him.

phrases.english: If the verse had repeated it,
it would be neither a disproof nor a support.
Now that the verse did not repeat it,
it supports him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is ריש לקיש, whom רבא set out to support.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אַהְדְּרֵיהּ קְרָא לָא תְּיוּבְתָּא וְלָא סִיַּיעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 and confirms רבא's proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the strength of a proof from omission
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוק could have explained a repeated תשומת יד, its omission proves nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Inclusion would have been neutral, but the actual omission supports ריש לקיש.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק's silence about תשומת יד supports ריש לקיש: without משיכה there is no acquisition.

steps.title: Does the verse really leave out the pledge case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 12. A ברייתא and רב's teaching show that the return פסוק does include תשומת יד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did the פסוק really not repeat תשומת יד? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון said, how do we know to apply the list above to the פסוק below? Because it says 'or anything about which he swore falsely.' And רב said this phrase comes to include תשומת יד in the duty to return.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the claim from Step 12 that the return פסוק left out תשומת יד. It brings a source showing that the פסוק does include it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 built support for ריש לקיש on the fact that תשומת יד is missing from the return פסוק. But the words 'או מכל אשר ישבע עליו לשקר' bring the whole earlier list, including תשומת יד, into the return פסוק. If so, the 'silence' that supported ריש לקיש seems to be gone.

keyTerms.meaning: A pledge or collateral put in someone's hand
From the earlier פסוק to the later פסוק

phrases.english: And did the verse not repeat the pledge?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Shimon said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִיתֵּן אֶת הָאָמוּר לְמַעְלָה לְמַטָּה,
phrases.english: From where do we know to apply what is stated above to what is stated below?
phrases.notes: 'Above' is the list of sins in ויקרא 5:21, which includes תשומת יד. 'Below' is the giving-back פסוק in 5:23.

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״אוֹ מִכֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִשָּׁבַע עָלָיו לַשֶּׁקֶר״,
phrases.english: As it is written: 'Or anything about which he has sworn falsely,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav said:
This comes to include the pledge in the duty to return.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְשׂוּמֶת יָד לָא אַהְדְּרֵיהּ קְרָא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in Step 12 that the פסוק was silent about תשומת יד.
steps.kashyaTarget: The argument from silence in Step 12
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A דרשה shows that the return פסוק does include תשומת יד, so it was not left out.

steps.title: At least it is not written openly
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק includes תשומת יד only through a דרשה. It never names it openly, so the support for ריש לקיש stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the פסוק did not repeat it openly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Yes, a דרשה includes תשומת יד, but the פסוק does not say it outright.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof for ריש לקיש rests on what the פסוק spells out clearly. The return פסוק (ויקרא 5:23) openly names גזלה, עושק and פקדון again, but it never names תשומת יד. תשומת יד comes in only through the extra words of 5:24, so the gap in the open wording still supports ריש לקיש.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the פסוק stands: תשומת יד is included only through a דרשה and is never written openly.

phrases.english: Openly, in any case,
the verse did not repeat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling apart open wording from a דרשה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The דרשה makes it as if תשומת יד is written in the return פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The proof depends on what is written openly, and תשומת יד is not.

steps.title: Where is the proof from a ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for support for ריש לקיש from a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this from a ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It now looks for support for ריש לקיש from a ברייתא, not from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the support came from reading the פסוק. Now the גמרא wants a ברייתא that shows the same idea: by Torah law, objects are acquired through משיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה

phrases.english: From a ברייתא, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the proof based on the פסוק to a proof from a ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A ברייתא that supports ריש לקיש's view that משיכה acquires by Torah law.

steps.title: The bathhouse case and רב's inference
steps.stepSummary: Paying a bathhouse attendant with הקדש money is מעילה right away. רב learns from this that when an object needs to be pulled, there is no מעילה until the משיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: if he gave הקדש money to a bathhouse attendant, he committed מעילה. רב said: this is only for a bathhouse attendant, where no pulling is needed. But for other things that need pulling, he does not commit מעילה until he pulls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא about a bathhouse attendant. Through רב's inference, this becomes support for ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעילה happens once the הקדש money is truly spent, meaning the deal is done. In a bathhouse there is nothing to pull, so the payment finishes the deal at once. But when buying an object, the deal is only done with משיכה, which shows that money alone does not acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: He committed מעילה, misuse of הקדש
Pulling an item to acquire it

steps.confusionAlert: The person paying is the one who commits מעילה. The question is simply when his deal is finished. With money alone, or only once he pulls the item?

phrases.english: As it is taught: if he gave it to a bathhouse attendant, he committed misuse,
phrases.notes: 'It' means a coin that belongs to הקדש, used to pay for the bath.

phrases.english: And Rav said: specifically a bathhouse attendant,
since there no pulling is lacking,
but other things, where pulling is lacking,
he does not commit misuse until he pulls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's view that by Torah law objects are acquired through משיכה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the bathhouse attendant, with רב's inference about objects that need pulling

steps.title: The barber case seems to contradict
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says that paying a barber with הקדש money is מעילה right away. But a barber's deal should need משיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: if he gave it to a barber, he committed מעילה. And a barber needs pulling for the haircut!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's inference. A barber case seems to work without משיכה, yet it still counts as מעילה right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said that when pulling is needed, there is no מעילה until the משיכה. But with a barber there is something to pull, and still the ברייתא says מעילה happens at once. That suggests money alone finishes the deal, which goes against the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The haircut, meaning the haircut tools

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: if he gave it to a barber, he committed misuse?
And with a barber, doesn't he need to pull the haircut?
phrases.notes: He means the barber's tools that are used for the haircut. Those would be the thing that gets pulled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's inference in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that when pulling is needed, there is no מעילה until the משיכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A barber case needs pulling, yet the ברייתא rules מעילה happens right away.

steps.title: The barber is a גוי
steps.stepSummary: The barber ברייתא is about a barber who is a גוי, and the משיכה rule does not apply to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A barber who is a גוי, who is not part of the משיכה system.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the barber ברייתא to a barber who is a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משיכה is how a deal is finished between Jews. A גוי is not part of that rule, so a deal with him is finished by the payment. That is why מעילה happens right away, and רב's inference about Jewish deals still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?

phrases.aramaic: בְּסַפָּר גּוֹי, דְּלָאו בַּר מְשִׁיכָה הוּא.
phrases.english: With a barber who is a גוי, who is not subject to pulling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a barber who is a גוי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The barber is Jewish, so money alone finished the deal even though pulling was needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The barber is a גוי, and the משיכה rule does not apply to him.

steps.title: A second ברייתא supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says that with a barber, there is no מעילה until the משיכה. The two ברייתות can only fit together if one is about a barber who is a גוי and the other about a Jewish barber.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way: if he gave it to a barber, a sailor, or any craftsman, he does not commit מעילה until he pulls. The two ברייתות contradict each other! Must we not learn from this: here it is a barber who is a גוי, and there it is a Jewish barber?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that clashes with the first barber ברייתא. It shows that the way to solve the clash is exactly the answer from Step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ברייתא says מעילה happens right away with a barber. The other says only after משיכה. They can only both be true if they are about different barbers: a גוי, where money finishes the deal, and a Jew, where משיכה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way, a supporting source

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
If he gave it to a barber, or to a sailor,
or to any craftsmen,
he does not commit misuse until he pulls.
They are difficult against each other.
Rather, must we not learn from it:

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בְּסַפָּר גּוֹי, כָּאן בְּסַפָּר יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: here, with a barber who is a גוי; there, with a Jewish barber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 18 with a second ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the first barber ברייתא is about a barber who is a גוי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A second ברייתא saying there is no מעילה until משיכה with a barber or craftsman, which clashes with the first unless they are about different barbers

steps.title: Yes, learn it from here
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the conclusion: a barber who is a גוי is different from a Jewish barber.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the answer and closes this part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the barber contradiction solved, רב's inference from the bathhouse ברייתא stands. Between Jews, an object is not acquired until משיכה, and this supports ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, a closing agreement

steps.whatToRemember: With a Jew, there is no מעילה until the משיכה, because only משיכה finishes the deal. With a גוי, the payment finishes it. This ברייתא gives support to ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the conclusion drawn in Step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The barber ברייתות are about a barber who is a גוי versus a Jewish barber, so רב's inference that משיכה is needed stands, supporting ריש לקיש.

steps.title: רב נחמן agrees that money acquires by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן holds that by Torah law, giving money acquires movable objects. This is the same view as רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said the same thing: by Torah law, money acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that רב נחמן agrees with the view that, by Torah law, paying money is enough to acquire movable things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וְכֵן ("and so") tells us this view was already said earlier in the sugya by רבי יוחנן. רב נחמן's statement adds weight to that side. The rule of משיכה (pulling) is then only a rule the חכמים added, and it is not the Torah-level way to acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: And so said: this introduces another אמורא who holds the same view.
By Torah law, as opposed to a rule the חכמים added
Money acquires: paying completes the purchase

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean that in practice money alone finishes the deal. The חכמים required משיכה. The question here is only what the Torah law is underneath.

phrases.english: And so said Rav Nachman,
phrases.notes: "And so" means he agrees with רבי יוחנן's view from earlier in the sugya.

phrases.english: by Torah law, money acquires.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the barber discussion, the גמרא goes back to the main argument and lists another אמורא who holds that money acquires by Torah law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By Torah law, paying money acquires movable property.

steps.title: לוי finds a ברייתא about paying a wholesaler
steps.stepSummary: לוי searched his collection of ברייתות and found that if someone paid a wholesaler with הקדש money, he is guilty of מעילה. This supports the view that money acquires by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי checked his collection of ברייתות and found: if he gave the הקדש coin to a wholesaler, he is guilty of מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof from a ברייתא that לוי found. Paying a wholesaler with הקדש money counts as מעילה right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer paid the wholesaler but did not pull the produce, and he is still guilty of מעילה. מעילה happens only when the הקדש money has really been used up in a completed deal. So the payment alone completed the deal, and that shows that by Torah law money acquires.

keyTerms.meaning: A wholesaler who sells produce in large amounts
He is guilty of מעילה, the misuse of הקדש property

steps.whatToRemember: There are two supports for "מעות קונות by Torah law": רב נחמן's statement, and לוי's ברייתא of the סיטון, where there is מעילה as soon as the money is paid, without משיכה.

phrases.english: And Levi checked it in his collection of baraitot and found:
If he gave it to a wholesaler, he is guilty of misusing consecrated property!
phrases.notes: "It" is the הקדש coin from the earlier cases. He paid it as a first payment, before pulling any produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After quoting רב נחמן's view, the גמרא backs it up with a written ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The view that by Torah law money acquires movable objects (רבי יוחנן and רב נחמן).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in לוי's collection: paying a סיטון with הקדש money is מעילה, even without משיכה.
